findings.body: When neither the checkout nor the searched history contains a story record, this condition allows work with no approval, and both subsequent hash checks are skipped. A manually created branch, or rewritten history that removes the approval record, can therefore send an unapproved brief to the full-access worker after committing status. The comment explicitly preserves this production exception for test fixtures. Require approval unconditionally, matching src/forge/task.py:137–139, and update those fixtures.
findings.title: Not done: 8. Refuse missing approval unconditionally

findings.body: The thread handler already captures the correct baseline in pending.start before acknowledging the conversation. This line replaces it with a fresh HEAD lookup after Codex has started executing: src/forge/codex_turn.py:138–139 starts the turn before emitting its ID. If Forge is delayed while the worker commits, the saved baseline includes that work, so the next fix round omits those commits and changes. Persist the previously captured pending.start instead of rereading HEAD.
findings.title: Not done: 7. Preserve the commit captured before the turn starts

findings.body: The test captures its expected start commit after the first work call returns, and the stub never commits during that turn. Consequently, using the previous turn's ending commit instead of its starting commit would still pass these delta assertions. Add a case that commits during the first turn and verifies that the next prompt includes that commit and its changes.

findings.body: The supplied walkthrough tests absent approval records, but does not exercise item 8's changed approved text, refusal before a status commit, reapproval, and replacement of the old conversation. Deleting approval records does not exercise the hash comparisons or approval-based conversation invalidation. Complete that user-facing sequence and record its observed results in the Functional check paragraph.

findings.body: This new lockfile is outside the permitted scope and introduces no dependency resolution needed by continuation, approval checks, or recovery. The SDK remains separately pinned and installed by Forge; pyproject.toml declares no project dependencies. Remove the unrelated lockfile from this change.
